title: U.S. House · Missouri's 1st District
area: St. Louis city and northern St. Louis County, including central and north St. Louis, Ferguson and Florissant.

context.text: Incumbent Wesley Bell, who won a special-primary contest against Cori Bush in 2024, defeated Bush again 59.2%-36.9% in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary, along with Alissa Murphy, Carl Harris Sr. and Carl Henderson. Paul Berry defeated Andrew Jones Jr. in the Republican primary, and Tom Schmitz advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Wesley Bell

priorities.text: Expand healthcare access, protect Medicaid and Medicare, and invest in public health research and mental health services.
Lower household energy costs and expand clean energy investment.
Advance diversion and rehabilitation programs as alternatives to incarceration, drawing on his background as a former prosecuting attorney.

positions.summary: Calls for ICE to be abolished and defunded and has introduced or cosponsored legislation to restrict ICE funding and require law enforcement officers to be identifiable.
positions.quote: Congressman Bell has been clear: ICE needs to be abolished and defunded, and the Trump Administration must be held accountable.

positions.summary: Cosponsors the Medicare for All Act and lists expanding healthcare access and protecting Medicaid and Medicare among his priorities.
positions.quote: Cosponsor of the Medicare for All Act

positions.summary: Lists expanding clean energy investment among his positions on environmental justice and energy affordability.
positions.quote: Congressman Bell supports: Lowering household energy costs Expanding clean energy investment Environmental remediation Disaster resilience and preparedness Modernizing infrastructure

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee; Health Care and Financial Services Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress.
Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (Strategic Forces Subcommittee; Tactical Air and Land Forces Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress.
Introduced the No ICE Ads Act to prohibit taxpayer-funded partisan ICE promotional advertising.
Introduced the Community First Pretrial Reform Act, creating a Department of Justice grant program to help local communities reduce unnecessary jail time.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals for incumbent Wesley Bell are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Paul Berry

priorities.text: Campaign website priorities include opposing abortion ("Pro Life Missouri"), defending Second Amendment rights, election integrity, border security, criminal-justice reform, school choice, and lowering taxes for seniors and workers.

candidates.researchNotes: Berry has not completed Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 Candidate Connection survey. His current campaign site (momadmaga.com) is focused on opposing socialism and the St. Louis city government and has no issues page; the two statements here come from his 2024 campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia, in third-person campaign copy rather than first-person quotes. No other stated positions on guide issues were found.

statements.quote: Championing the sanctity of life, Paul advocates for policies that protect and value every unborn child.
statements.context: From his 2024 campaign website, as reproduced on Ballotpedia; his current site (momadmaga.com) has no issues page

statements.quote: Empowering choice in education. Paul champions diverse school options for all.
statements.context: From his 2024 campaign website, as reproduced on Ballotpedia; his current site (momadmaga.com) has no issues page

candidates.name: Tom Schmitz
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

priorities.text: Separate healthcare from government in favor of a free-market healthcare system.
priorities.quote: We need separation of healthcare and state

priorities.text: Change to a foreign policy of non-interventionism and end foreign aid.
priorities.quote: We need decisive change to a foreign policy of peace and non-interventionism.

priorities.text: End the war on drugs and legalize currently controlled substances.
priorities.quote: Currently controlled substances should be legalized and treated the same under the law as alcohol.

positions.summary: Advocates separating healthcare from government and a free-market system in place of government-run coverage.
positions.quote: We need separation of healthcare and state, a liberated healthcare system free from government coercion and control, a free-market system which will drive down prices, inspire innovation, and increase quality through competition.

positions.summary: Says funding a child's education is solely the parents' responsibility and calls for removing government from education.
positions.quote: The management and funding of a child's education is the responsibility of the parents of that child and no one else.

positions.summary: Says gun-rights protections should be vigilantly defended and that the expansion of red flag laws should be resisted.
positions.quote: We must resist the expansion of "red flag" laws, which are a dangerous slippery slope toward government obtaining the power to disarm American Citizens at will and without any semblance of due process.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions, statements and priorities come from the issues page of his campaign website (tomschmitzforliberty.com). He has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. No stated position found on rent, minimum wage, tariffs or police funding beyond what is listed.

statements.quote: I believe that innovations in medical technology unleashed by the free market can make abortion obsolete in our society.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: In addition, this government has failed to effectively fight global climate change by severely blunting the development of nuclear power.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: The ideal in a free society without compulsory taxation or government welfare programs is that immigrants would be able to move across borders as freely as possible.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page
